blocks.html: A WhatsApp BSP (Business Solution Provider) is a company officially vetted by Meta to give businesses access to the WhatsApp Business API, with tooling for onboarding, automation, analytics and support on top. Choosing the right one in 2026 comes down to seven things: pricing transparency, per-message markup, support SLA, India business-hours coverage, integrations, official BSP status, and security/compliance. This checklist walks each one. The stakes are real: your BSP controls your per-message cost, your uptime, and how fast you can launch. A cheap-looking provider with a hidden markup or weekend-only support can cost more than a transparent one. Use the checklist below on every provider you shortlist — and yes, on Ojiva AI too. If you are still deciding between the free app and the API in the first place, start with WhatsApp Business App vs API.

sections.heading: What Is a WhatsApp BSP (Business Solution Provider)?

blocks.html: You cannot buy the WhatsApp Business API directly from Meta. Instead, Meta authorises Business Solution Providers to onboard businesses, provision phone numbers, get display names and templates approved, and deliver messages through the platform. The BSP is also where you get the dashboard, chatbot, team inbox and integrations that make the API usable day to day.
In short, the BSP is your gateway to WhatsApp — and the quality of that gateway determines your cost, reliability and speed to launch.

sections.heading: BSP vs Tech Provider: What's the Difference?

blocks.html: In 2026 you will see two labels: "BSP" and "tech provider." An official BSP has a direct, vetted partnership with Meta. A tech provider builds software on top of the API and sometimes resells through a BSP. Both can work, but the distinction matters for support and reliability — with an official BSP, there is no extra middle layer between you and the platform.

items.title: Ask directly:
items.desc: "Are you an official Meta BSP, or do you resell through one?" The answer tells you who actually owns your reliability and support.

blocks.html: Score every shortlisted provider against these seven criteria. Weight them by what matters most for your use case — a high-volume marketer cares most about markup; a bank cares most about compliance and uptime.

items.title: Pricing transparency:
items.desc: Can they show Meta's base rate and their own markup separately, in INR, with GST stated? Bundled, vague pricing usually hides a high markup.

items.title: Per-message markup:
items.desc: What percentage do they add over Meta rates — and is there a platform fee on top? Compare the all-in cost per marketing and utility message, not the headline.

items.title: Support SLA:
items.desc: Is there a written response-time SLA and a named contact, or only email tickets? When a campaign or OTP flow breaks, response time is revenue.

items.title: India business-hours coverage:
items.desc: Is support in your timezone and language? An India-based team beats an overseas helpdesk when you need help at 11 a.m. IST.

items.title: Integrations:
items.desc: Native connectors for your CRM and store — Shopify, Zoho, Salesforce, HubSpot — plus a clean REST API and webhooks. Integration gaps become manual work forever.

items.title: Security & compliance:
items.desc: AES-256 encryption, DPDP Act and GDPR alignment, and recognised standards (SOC 2, ISO 27001). Essential for banking, healthcare and any regulated data.

items.title: Reliability & scale:
items.desc: A real uptime SLA (99.9%+), proven delivery, and the ability to scale messaging tiers as you grow without re-onboarding.

sections.heading: Pricing Transparency: How to Read a BSP Quote (2026)

blocks.html: Since India moved to per-message pricing on 1 January 2026, a BSP quote should break into three parts: Meta's rate, the BSP's markup, and GST. If a provider cannot show you this breakdown, treat it as a red flag.

items.title: Compare all-in, not headline:
items.desc: A provider with a low platform fee but a 35% message markup can cost more than one with a small fee and 15% markup. Model your real monthly volume per category.

blocks.html: These warning signs separate a partner you can scale on from one you will regret.

items.title: Opaque pricing:
items.desc: Won't separate Meta rate from markup, or quotes only "per conversation" under the old model.

items.title: No real support:
items.desc: Ticket-only support, no SLA, no India-hours coverage, no named contact for enterprise accounts.

items.title: Integration gaps:
items.desc: No native connector for your CRM or store, and a thin or undocumented API.

items.title: Vague on BSP status or compliance:
items.desc: Can't confirm official Meta BSP status, or dodges questions on DPDP, encryption and data handling.

sections.heading: Questions to Ask Every BSP Before You Sign

blocks.html: The checklist tells you what to score; these are the exact questions that surface the truth in a sales call. Vague answers are an answer.

items.title: "What's your exact markup, and is there a platform fee?"
items.desc: You want a number in INR, separate from Meta's rate — not "competitive pricing".

items.title: "What's your uptime and support SLA in writing?"
items.desc: Ask for the document, the response time, and a named contact for your account.

items.title: "Where is my data stored, and which standards do you hold?"
items.desc: DPDP alignment, data residency, SOC 2 / ISO 27001 — essential for regulated data.

items.title: "Can I keep my number and leave cleanly?"
items.desc: Confirm number portability and the exit process before you're locked in.

items.title: "Who drafts templates, and how fast do they get approved?"
items.desc: Approval speed decides how quickly you can launch and iterate.

items.title: Model your real mix:

sections.heading: Hidden Costs to Watch in a BSP Contract

blocks.html: The headline rate is rarely the whole bill. These line items quietly inflate cost — ask about each before signing.

items.title: Setup & onboarding fees:
items.desc: Some charge a one-time fee to get you live. Fair if disclosed — a red flag if buried.

items.title: Per-agent seat fees:
items.desc: A low platform fee can hide a charge for every inbox user — costly as your team grows.

items.title: Minimum monthly commitment:
items.desc: A floor you pay even in slow months — check it against your lowest-volume season.

items.title: Overage & add-on charges:
items.desc: Extra fees for going over a tier, for the chatbot, or for premium support — confirm what's included vs billed separately.

sections.heading: Frequently Asked Questions: Choosing a WhatsApp BSP in India

items.a: A WhatsApp Business Solution Provider (BSP) is a company officially vetted by Meta to give businesses access to the WhatsApp Business API, along with tooling for onboarding, automation, analytics, compliance and support.

items.q: How do I choose the best WhatsApp BSP in India?
items.a: Score each provider on pricing transparency, per-message markup, support SLA and India business-hours coverage, CRM and e-commerce integrations, official Meta BSP status, security and DPDP compliance, and delivery reliability. The best BSP is the one that scores well on the criteria that matter most for your use case.

items.q: What is a typical WhatsApp BSP markup in India?
items.a: Most BSPs add a 15–35% per-message markup over Meta's base rates, or charge a fixed monthly platform fee, plus 18% GST. A transparent BSP shows the Meta rate and its own markup separately rather than bundling them.

items.q: What is the difference between a BSP and a tech provider?
items.a: An official BSP has a direct, vetted partnership with Meta to provide WhatsApp Business API access. A tech provider builds tools on top of the API, sometimes reselling through a BSP. For reliability and direct support, an official BSP is usually the safer choice.

items.q: How do I verify a WhatsApp BSP is official?
items.a: Check Meta's public Business Partner directory, confirm the provider verifies your business in Meta Business Manager, and ask for proof of official BSP status before signing.

items.q: Does a WhatsApp BSP handle DLT registration?
items.a: WhatsApp does not use DLT — that is for SMS. A good full-stack provider will, however, handle DLT for any SMS you send alongside WhatsApp, and manage Meta verification and template approval for WhatsApp.
